questions.prompt: A VM runs in West Europe. A standard ARM move transfers it to an existing resource group whose metadata location is North Europe. No regional relocation is performed. Which location pair is correct after the move?

options.text: VM: West Europe; destination group metadata: North Europe.
options.explanation: An ARM scope move preserves the VM region. The existing destination group keeps its own metadata location.

options.text: VM: North Europe; destination group metadata: North Europe.
options.explanation: Group membership does not relocate the VM to the metadata region.

options.text: VM: West Europe; destination group metadata: West Europe.
options.explanation: The VM keeps West Europe, but its location does not change the destination group metadata.

options.text: VM: North Europe; destination group metadata: West Europe.
options.explanation: Neither location is exchanged: the VM region remains West Europe and the group metadata remains North Europe.

questions.prompt: A VM, its NIC, disks, and virtual network will be moved from subscription A to subscription B using a direct ARM cross-subscription move. Which TWO statements describe requirements for this move? Evaluate each statement individually.

options.text: Subscriptions A and B must belong to the same Microsoft Entra tenant.
options.explanation: Direct cross-subscription ARM moves require matching tenant IDs; they do not cross tenant boundaries.

options.text: The virtual network and its dependent resources must move with the VM.
options.explanation: The VM move limitation requires the VNet and dependent resources to move together across subscriptions.

options.text: The NIC can remain in subscription A while the attached VM moves to B.
options.explanation: The cross-subscription dependency requirement does not permit leaving the attached NIC behind.

options.text: The destination group metadata location must match the VM region.
options.explanation: A resource group can contain resources in other regions. Matching metadata location is not this move requirement.

questions.prompt: A VM named vm-app moves from rg-old to rg-new in the same subscription. A script still requests its previous ARM resource ID and receives ResourceNotFound. The VM is visible in rg-new, the move is complete, and the script identity has the required access there. Which change addresses the failure?

options.text: Replace rg-old with rg-new in the resource ID used by the script.
options.explanation: The resource-group segment changes during the move. The old path no longer identifies the VM at its current scope.

options.text: Acquire a new access token while continuing to use the old resource ID.
options.explanation: Authentication refresh does not replace the stale scope segment. Access at the new scope is already established.

options.text: Replace vm-app in the ID with the guest operating-system hostname.
options.explanation: The ARM resource name remains vm-app. The guest hostname does not select its resource-group scope.

options.text: Replace the subscription segment while continuing to use rg-old.
options.explanation: The subscription did not change; the stale segment is the resource group.
